subject.title: Owner-signed responsibility gates for assistant memory, actions, skills, and evidence reuse

question: Should OpenClaw define a core durable owner-confirmed responsibility lifecycle for memory/evidence reuse, or keep this as plugin/ClawHub integration work until a narrower core API gap is proven?
rationale: The request crosses persistent memory trust, plugin SDK semantics, skill/action approval gates, evidence reuse, and public config, so automation cannot safely choose the security boundary or product ownership model.

options.title: Sponsor a core/plugin-SDK security design
options.body: Define the minimal durable states, owner-confirmation semantics, revocation behavior, and plugin API contract before accepting implementation PRs.

options.title: Split into narrower canonical issues
options.body: Keep this as an umbrella and move execution-gate, memory-trust, provenance, and skill-governance pieces to separately reviewable issues like the existing related threads.

options.title: Route external responsibility-chain tools to ClawHub first
options.body: Ask SCBKR or UMP-style integrations to ship as plugins/bundles until they identify a specific missing OpenClaw extension point.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core/plugin-SDK security design
recommendation.body: Define the minimal durable states, owner-confirmation semantics, revocation behavior, and plugin API contract before accepting implementation PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: The central decision spans memory host architecture and approval/security boundaries where Peter has the clearest feature-history signal.
